name: Salesforce Tower
note: OSM maps it three ways: the outline way/431972186, a duplicate outline way/1560173288, and TEN `building:part` wedges that between them are the whole tower. The bake drops an outline whose parts cover it (tools/bake.ts, `superseded`), so neither outline is in the package and the entry, naming only those two, selected nothing — the parts fell through to the classifier, which gave them `skyscraper`, and the tallest building in the city rendered as a plain glass box. Fixed by hand with an explicit lat/lon + size until BUGS.md #100 was fixed systemically: an entry naming a superseded outline now claims every part carrying its id and is fitted to the union of the grounded ones, which measures 54.3 × 54.6 m 2 m from the hand-written point. So the ten part ids, the point and the size are gone; naming them would be WRONG now, because a part that resolves is fitted to itself and each of these is a ~250 m² wedge. `front: 137` turns the model's plan to the downtown grid.

name: Moscone Center South
note: CORRECTION 2026-09-23: the `mosconeHall` preset that stood here (a 20 m glass box from ring-tower.ts, lowered to 8 earlier the same day) is REMOVED, not lowered again — at any height it stood where `mosconeSouthDeck`'s own surface and parapet already are (sf/yerba-buena.ts, a separate lat/lon landmark that already caps this way properly) and blocked the open Howard skybridge's landing (docs/MOSCONE-SOUTH.md). This entry now names no `procedural`/`file` at all — a PLACEHOLDER (render/landmarks.ts's own third kind): the raw OSM box is still taken out of the bake (`replacedIds` counts placeholders, not only replacements), but nothing new is built in its place, since `mosconeSouthDeck` is what actually stands here. The real hall this way represents is level 1, mostly below the deck and visible only from Howard Street; the above-ground Howard-facing mass belongs to a different way (way/426708093, queued manual, not this entry's).

_why: DUPLICATE. It sat at the same lat/lon as the procedural `ghirardelliSign` (which was rebuilt from a photograph on 2026-09-22), 12 m above it at offset y 36 against y 24 — and the owner reports it lies FACING THE SKY, which makes the good sign unreadable behind it. Note why it only appeared now: landmarks.ts's modelUrl was fixed so that a file beginning "models/" resolves from the site root, and both this and Ripley's had been 404ing silently. Reinstate by restoring `name`/`file`/`lat`/`lon`/`front`/`size`/`offset` once the glTF's orientation is right and one of the two is removed.
